scope: Primary literature/code source register for MICROSTRUCTURE_ROUND1.md. Source claims motivate mechanisms only; transfer to the anonymized challenge stream is untested.

sources.title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
sources.version_note: arXiv first submitted 2010, revised 2011; journal reference: Journal of Financial Econometrics 12(1), 47–88 (Winter 2014).
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the arXiv paper page and inspected its title, authors, submission/version record, journal reference, and abstract.
sources.source_claim: In the studied NYSE data, short-interval price changes were mainly driven by best-bid/ask order-flow imbalance; their measured impact was approximately linear and inversely related to market depth.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: A small causal event-state summary may preserve some event-flow information in the challenge features.
counterevidence_and_limits: The study uses identified exchange events and a best-level interpretation absent from the challenge's anonymized feature codes.
Local audit evidence reports no reproducible forecast gain for a broad i0 order-flow feature block; contemporaneous impact is not future-label alpha.

sources.title: Econometric Analysis of Discrete-Valued Irregularly-Spaced Financial Transactions Data Using a New Autoregressive Conditional Multinomial Model
sources.version_note: Author-hosted UC San Diego discussion paper 98-10, February/April 1998; this paper discusses the Engle–Russell ACD model and its relation to arrival-time/mark dynamics.
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened and inspected the 33-page author-hosted PDF, including its title page, abstract, introduction, and description of ACD arrival times and duration-dependent transition probabilities.
sources.source_claim: The authors describe the ACD framework for irregular event intervals and a marked-process view in which price-transition probabilities may depend on realized/expected duration, volume, and spread.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: The row-step interval between observed feature-change events may contain a useful causal rate-normalized state.
counterevidence_and_limits: The source studies financial transaction arrival times with transaction marks, while this challenge provides row steps and anonymous feature groups rather than verified trades or timestamps.
Past per-field age proposals only established added representation resolution, not predictive value.

sources.title: Forecasting High Frequency Order Flow Imbalance
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the arXiv paper page and inspected title, authors, version/date, and abstract.
sources.source_claim: The paper models bid/ask OFI dependence with Hawkes processes and reports the best OFI forecast among its tested models for a sum-of-exponentials kernel on NSE tick data.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: A few exponential traces over observed feature-event families may approximate useful event clustering without a large sequence model.
counterevidence_and_limits: The dependent variable is OFI distribution, not the challenge's two future-price labels.
The paper's stated best method and dataset result do not imply lift here; broad local flow features were already negative/null in forecast tests.

sources.title: Inferring Microscopic Financial Information from the Long Memory in Market-Order Flow: A Quantitative Test of the Lillo-Mike-Farmer Model
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the APS publisher page and inspected title, author list, publication date, abstract, and article text outline.
sources.source_claim: Using long high-frequency TSE account-level data, the authors report power-law persistence in market-order signs and quantitative agreement between observed sign-correlation decay and the Lillo-Mike-Farmer model.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: A persistent side-activity proxy in the challenge might need a longer memory kernel than a few short event-age features.
counterevidence_and_limits: The challenge does not expose participant identity or verified buy/sell market-order signs.
Long memory in inputs can be offset by liquidity/size effects and does not by itself establish directional predictability.

sources.title: Cross-Impact of Order Flow Imbalance in Equity Markets
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the arXiv paper page and inspected the title, authors, revision history, and abstract.
sources.source_claim: The authors report that integrated multi-level OFI improves impact explanation; lagged cross-asset OFI improves short-horizon return forecasts and its effect decays rapidly, while contemporaneous cross-impact adds little after own OFI in their study.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: A lag-profile of observed i1 changes might contain information not represented by a static i1 block.
counterevidence_and_limits: The study uses many identified equity assets and OFI; the challenge has one auxiliary instrument, anonymous features, and no i1 target.
The local audit reports no reproducible gain from its tested static i1 cross-impact block; a prior event-time i1 proposal is also an explicit overlap.

sources.title: On Covariance Estimation of Non-synchronously Observed Diffusion Processes
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Retrieved the actual author-hosted PDF text, including title, abstract, journal issue, and the overlapping-interval covariance estimator formula. A later direct-open attempt timed out; the inspected content was the PDF text itself, not a secondary summary.
sources.source_claim: The paper proposes estimating covariance from products of increments whose observation intervals overlap, avoiding forced synchronization of nonsynchronous processes.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: Explicit event-order or lag handling may be safer than assuming feature changes in the two instruments are perfectly aligned in event time.
counterevidence_and_limits: The estimator is for processes observed with actual timestamps; this challenge documents row order but not exchange timestamps, so the estimator cannot be applied literally.
Only two synchronized row records are exposed at each step; inferred event timing is a proxy, not true asynchrony correction.

sources.title: HLOB -- Information Persistence and Structure in Limit Order Books
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the arXiv paper page and inspected title, authors, version history, and abstract.
sources.source_claim: HLOB uses an information-filtering graph to represent dependencies among volume levels and evaluates the model against alternatives on three NASDAQ LOB datasets.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: There may be stable pairwise interactions among named challenge feature components even when adjacent indices do not denote adjacent depth.
counterevidence_and_limits: HLOB's graph is built for interpreted volume levels; challenge component identifiers do not guarantee level order.
Local audit notes HLOB/bilinear proposals in documents but no proven execution result; the actual edge structure may not be stable here.

sources.title: Deep Learning Meets Queue-Reactive: A Framework for Realistic Limit Order Book Simulation
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the arXiv page and inspected title, authors, submission date, and abstract.
sources.source_claim: The MDQR simulator extends queue-reactive modeling with cross-queue dependencies, richer market state, and order-size distributions, and reports reproducing selected market stylized facts on Bund futures data.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: A predictive event effect may depend on the current observed feature state, rather than being useful as a context-free flow signal.
counterevidence_and_limits: The paper evaluates realistic simulation/stylized facts, not this competition's pooled weighted Pearson objective.
Challenge queue semantics and level ordering are not supplied; state conditioning must preserve raw feature identities and avoid physical queue claims.

sources.title: Limit Order Book Event Stream Prediction with Diffusion Model
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the arXiv paper page and inspected title, authors, version date, and abstract.
sources.source_claim: LOBDIF models future LOB event time and event type jointly with a diffusion-based event-stream model and reports results on three real-world assets.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: A small auxiliary objective over observable event family and row-step waiting time may shape a useful causal representation.
counterevidence_and_limits: The primary task is event generation/distribution prediction, not direct price-direction scoring.
A generic next-row pretraining idea is already present in local history as queued/unverified, and earlier event heads had mixed or null outcomes.

sources.title: Extracting Information from the Signature of a Financial Data Stream
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the arXiv page and inspected its title, author list, revision record, and abstract.
sources.source_claim: The authors use path-signature coordinates to summarize financial streams and report examples involving market behavior and execution-algorithm impact classification.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: Low-degree path terms could encode event ordering and interactions among a few challenge streams.
counterevidence_and_limits: The reported examples and stream sampling differ from this challenge's online per-row callback.
A mathematically expressive signature can be redundant, noisy, or too costly; no transfer to pooled WP is established.

sources.title: Latent Continuum of Regimes in Limit Order Book Dynamics
sources.version_note: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-10-05, revised 2026-10-06 (v2); preprint as of this register date.
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the arXiv page and inspected submission/revision dates, author, title, and full abstract.
sources.source_claim: On EURO STOXX 50 futures, the preprint studies covariance-state geometry and reports a low-dimensional continuous state; it reports stronger out-of-sample performance at a macro regime tier than finer discrete tiers.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: A continuous online covariance summary may be more robust than fixed regime categories for this sequence-local state.
counterevidence_and_limits: This is a newly posted preprint, not established consensus, and uses 30–60 second aggregated futures observations rather than this anonymized 20,000-step stream.
The preprint reports that fine-grained regime tiers fail to generalize; it does not establish a prediction gain for this challenge.

sources.title: Fast Online Changepoint Detection via Functional Pruning CUSUM Statistics
sources.version_note: arXiv first submitted 2021-10-15, revised 2022-07-27 (v3); JMLR journal reference 2023.
sources.source_type: primary paper / arXiv preprint with journal reference
sources.actual_source_content_checked: Opened the arXiv page and inspected title, authors, abstract, submission/version dates, and JMLR journal reference.
sources.source_claim: FOCuS combines CUSUM-like mean-shift detectors over window/change sizes, with a theoretical per-iteration cost logarithmic in observations and reported server-anomaly applications.
sources.local_transfer_assumption: A bounded one-sided change alarm over normalized per-sequence feature innovations could gate a slow predictor state.
counterevidence_and_limits: Its application is server telemetry, not market or financial forecasting; the source validates detection efficiency, not predictive value.
Routine market event clusters may trigger too many alarms; calibration on independent synthetic shifts does not show target quality.
